device: vitrified-bond aluminum-oxide grinding wheel for titanium alloy parts
failure_mode: wheel loading and glazing causing thermal damage to the workpiece
failure: Documented manufacturing problem: when grinding titanium alloys (Ti-6Al-4V) with conventional aluminum-oxide wheels, titanium chips adhere to the wheel's abrasive grains and bond (wheel loading); the loaded wheel stops cutting, friction rises, the wheel glazes, and the workpiece surface temperature spikes — producing tensile residual stresses, alpha-case burn, microcracking, and scrapped expensive aerospace parts. Titanium's low thermal conductivity and chemical reactivity with abrasive make this worse than steel grinding. Qualitative engineering-literature context; no fabricated statistics (retrieval must custody the evidence).
constraint: The intervention must not require a different machine tool, must keep wheel cost within 3x of conventional wheels, must not introduce combustible or toxic coolant chemistry, and must preserve the achievable surface integrity requirements for aerospace structural titanium.

sources.problem_basis: engineering-literature qualitative context; no fabricated statistics
